content.title: Men’s March Madness 2026 First Four wins for Prairie View, Miami (OH): Live updates and reaction
content.text: Historic victory for Prairie View books matchup with defending champions Florida Gators Eian Elmer celebrates during Miami (OH) RedHawks’ win over SMU Mustangs Getty ImagesMen’s March Madness — Latest The First Four of the men’s NCAA Tournament has concluded tonight in Dayton, Ohio.It was a historic night for (16) Prairie View A&M as the Panthers sealed their first NCAA Tournament win, beating (16) Lehigh Mountain Hawks 67-55 with a strong second-half effort. It booked a matchup with (1) Florida Gators.Then rounding off the First Four, (11) Miami (Ohio) RedHawks proved too strong for (11) SMU Mustangs as they sealed an 89-79 victory — the program’s first NCAA Tournament win since 1999. Sixth seed Tennessee now awaits Miami.Follow all the action, reaction and analysis live below. Share your thoughts: live@theathletic.comSKIP ADVERTISEMENTAdvertisementMen’s NCAA Tournament consensus bracket predictionsStill haven’t filled out your bracket yet? No worries, me neither.Before you make your final picks, make sure to check out The Athletic’s staff consensus predictions for the men’s NCAA Tournament.The first round begins tomorrow (12: 15 p.m. ET) as No. 8 Ohio State faces No. 9 TCU.Michigan, Iowa State favored in Midwest regionWho will conquer the Midwest region? According to The Athletic’s 2026 men’s NCAA Tournament projections, Michigan and Iowa State have the best odds to get it done. Favorites to win the Midwest region Updated March 26, 2026 at 5:29 PM Men’s March Madness 2026 First Four wins for Prairie View, Miami (OH): Live updates and reaction - The Athletic Thursday’s games for the Midwest region Getty ImagesThere will be two games played in the Midwest region on Thursday:(16) Howard vs. (1) Michigan — 7:10 p.m. ET(9) Saint Louis vs. (8) Georgia — 9:45 p.m. ETGators favored to win South regionAhead of the start of the first round tomorrow afternoon, let’s check out the favorites to win the South region — headlined by the defending national champion Florida Gators … Favorites to win the West region Updated March 26, 2026 at 5:29 PM Men’s March Madness 2026 First Four wins for Prairie View, Miami (OH): Live updates and reaction - The AthleticMen’s March Madness 2026 First Four wins for Prairie View, Miami (OH): Live updates and reaction - The Athletic Thursday’s games for the South region Getty ImagesThere will be six games played in the South region on Thursday:(13) Troy vs. (4) Nebraska — 12:40 p.m. ET(12) McNeese vs. (5) Vanderbilt — 3:15 p.m. ET(11) VCU vs. (6) North Carolina — 6:50 p.m. ET(14) Penn vs. (3) Illinois — 9:25 p.m. ET(10) Texas A&M vs. (7) Saint Mary’s — 7:35 p.m. ET(15) Idaho vs. (2) Houston — 10:10 p.m. ETSKIP ADVERTISEMENTAdvertisementIllinois’ defense needs to improve Getty ImagesNo.3 Illinois, who went 24-8 this season, takes on No. 14 Penn at 9:25 p.m. ET on Thursday in Greenville, N.C.The Balkan Bloc has made the Illini the second-best offense in college basketball, one that ranks third nationally in offensive rebounding percentage, sixth in free-throw percentage (78.9), 10th in turnover percentage and 18th in 2-point percentage (58.2). Brad Underwood’s team has been less consistent from 3 but four players — Keaton Wagler, David Mirkovic, Jake Davis and Ben Humrichous — shoot at least 35 percent from deep. That means Illinois has as many ways to beat you offensively as anyone in the field. However, there’s a reason the Illini have lost four overtime games — all by one possession — since Feb. 7: it’s a defense that puts next-to-no pressure on opponents.Houston to make another deep run? Getty ImagesNo. 2 Houston, who went 38-6 this season, takes on No. 15 Idaho at 10:10 p.m. ET on Thursday in Oklahoma City, OK.Why the Cougars can win it all: Because they have a coach, Kelvin Sampson, and a core relentlessly determined to rebound from last season’s national championship collapse. Sampson, 70, got within a possession of a title last April, only for his Coogs to not even get off a potential game-winning shot. But with multiple starters back — including graduate guard Emanuel Sharp, who (literally) dropped the ball on UH’s final possession against Florida — Sampson has a squad good enough and motivated enough to accomplish what last season’s couldn’t.Houston is one of five teams with a top-15 adjusted offensive and defensive efficiency ranking, per KenPom, with more balance than a typical Sampson team.The concerns: A lack of proven interior scoring, as neither defensive guru JoJo Tugler nor five-star freshman Chris Cenac Jr. is a reliable producer on an every-game basis. Without that consistent paint threat, Houston’s guards occasionally get caught bombing away from 3, which can lead to long scoring droughts — a potentially fatal flow given the low number of possessions in Coogs games.Can Michigan limit turnovers? Getty ImagesNo. 1 Michigan, who went 31-3 this season, takes on No. 16 Howard at 7:10 p.m. ET on Thursday in Buffalo, NY.Why the Wolverines can win it all: Because who says you can’t play — and win — with three giants on the court at the same time? Dusty May’s first two seasons with the Wolverines have been defined by his creativity utilizing unique bigs, and he’s deployed Michigan’s towering frontcourt trio to build the No. 1 defense in adjusted efficiency. That starts with 7-3 center Aday Mara, whose pterodactyl-like wingspan makes it near impossible to score against Michigan inside. Then there’s 6-9 battering ram Morez Johnson Jr. and 6-9 Swiss Army knife Yaxel Lendeborg — the Big Ten Player of the Year, and the best transfer in the sport. Both are top 200 nationally in block rate, per KenPom. Offensively, those three are just as potent. Mara is a passing savant who can see over everyone and who, combined with point guard Elliot Cadeau, makes Michigan one of the top teams in the field at sharing the ball. PThe concerns: Turnovers, and a tendency to go cold from 3 at inopportune times. The Wolverines give it away on 16.9 percent of their possessions, per KenPom, a sub-150 rate nationally. And that issue is only exacerbated by the fact reserve guard L.J. Cason, one of the team’s primary ballhandlers off the bench, tore an ACL in late February and is out for the NCAA Tournament. Michigan makes 36 percent of its 3s overall with Cadeau, freshman Trey McKenney and senior Nimari Burnett all over 37 percent individually, but shot only 28.4 percent from deep in its three losses this season.Arizona favored in West regionIs this the year the Arizona Wildcats get back to the national championship game?The Athletic’s 2026 men’s NCAA Tournament projections indicate a quality opportunity to do so.Favorites to win the West region Updated March 18, 2026 at 4:17 AM Thursday’s games for the West region Getty ImagesThere will be four games played in the West region on Thursday:(13) Hawai’i vs. (4) Arkansas — 4:25 p.m. ET(12) High Point vs. (5) Wisconsin — 1:50 p.m. ET(11) Texas vs. (6) BYU — 7:25 p.m. ET(14) Kennesaw State vs. (3) Gonzaga — 10 p.m. ETSKIP ADVERTISEMENTAdvertisementWill Duke represent the East region?The East region is loaded and even still, according to the odds, the Duke Blue Devils are the resounding favorite to win this section of the bracket.Favorites to win the East region Updated March 26, 2026 at 5:29 PM Chandler will not play for Siena Imagn ImagesOne of the strangest situations involving any NCAA Tournament team unfolded in relative anonymity last week amid conference championship week — but now Siena (16) is in the Big Dance, the Saints’ plight deserves more attention.Wing Antonio Chandler started the team’s first 29 games but was suddenly ruled ineligible in late February, and his multiple legal attempts to return to play have failed.“He won’t be available,” Siena coach Gerry McNamara said Wednesday, adding Chandler’s situation had “concluded.”Chandler’s college career began in 2019-20 at Division-II Franklin Pierce, where he played 58 games in four seasons due to multiple serious injuries. He transferred to NAIA Jamestown for the 2023-24 season, and later to Division-II Southern Connecticut for 2024-25. Due to injuries and the COVID pandemic, Chandler made his Division-I debut with Siena this season where he averaged 7.3 points and 5.6 rebounds for the MAAC champions.When the team submitted its roster to the MAAC tournament, Chandler’s eligibility was flagged and he was deemed unable to play. Chandler originally filed a complaint on March 4 in an effort to re-establish eligibility, but it was denied five days later. Chandler officially discontinued the suit on Wednesday, according to court briefings. McNamara said:💬 “If you go back and look at his story and where he came from and how he ended up playing one year of Division-I basketball with us, it’s a good story. “It’s a shame it ended the way it did, but I’m really proud of him and really proud of our guys in terms of how they handled the situation, rallying around their brother and being there for him.”With Chandler done for the season, Iowa transfer Riley Mulvey has started the Saints’ last four games in his place — averaging seven points and 9.5 rebounds per game.Siena is set to face No. 1 Duke at 2:50 p.m. ET on Thursday in Greenville, N.C.Can Duke keep dominating? Getty ImagesNo. 1 Duke, who went 32-2 this season, takes on No. 16 Siena at 2:50 p.m. ET on Thursday in Greenville, N.C.Why the Blue Devils can win it all: Because they have the best player in college basketball, freshman superstar Cameron Boozer, whose impact on winning is borderline supernatural. The 6-foot-9 forward is the ultimate mismatch, as capable of pouring in 3s — at a 40.9 percent clip this season — as using his 250-pound frame to bully opponents in the post.Beyond Boozer, Jon Scheyer’s team is incredibly balanced, and one of just two teams nationally that rank top five in adjusted offensive and defensive efficiency. Before recent injuries to starters Caleb Foster and Patrick Ngongba, this squad had a better net rating than last season’s Final Four group — which was second-best in KenPom’s database, dating to 1997.The concerns: Health … for the second straight postseason. Only this March, the Blue Devils’ injuries are much more consequential. Foster, Duke’s point guard and most veteran player, is out for the “foreseeable” future after breaking his right foot on March 7. There’s a chance he returns if the Blue Devils make the Final Four, but how effective will he be? Ngongba’s situation is only slightly rosier, with the starting center sitting out last week’s ACC tournament with lingering foot soreness. Scheyer said he’s progressing well, but will he be available the first weekend? Duke might not need him to make the Sweet 16, but it certainly will to win it all.Thursday’s games for the East region Getty ImagesThere will be four games played in the East region on Thursday:(9) TCU vs. (8) Ohio State — 12:15 p.m. ET(11) South Florida vs. (6) Louisville — 1:30 p.m. ET(16) Siena vs. (1) Duke — 2:50 p.m. ET(14) North Dakota State vs. (3) Michigan State — 4:05 p.m. ETSKIP ADVERTISEMENTAdvertisementICYMI: Up next for Prairie View A&M Getty ImagesThe reward for tonight’s early First Four matchup winner Prairie View A&M: a matchup against the defending national champions, the Florida Gators, at 9:25 p.m. ET on Friday.The Gators started off the season slow with four losses in their first nine games, but they have rounded into form and won the SEC’s regular season title. Florida returns head coach Todd Golden, forward Thomas Haugh and center Rueben Chinyelu from last year’s championship run and ranks 12th in the nation in points per game.THIS is what March is all about!The passion of Travis Steele and his squad is palpable, even through a screen.Stats comparison from Miami (OH)-SMU Getty ImagesOne statistic stands out from the others in the box score: the 3-pointers. The RedHawks attempted 41 and made 16, setting best marks for the First Four. Here are how the two teams stacked up statistically …FGMiami (OH): 29-64SMU: 31-653FGMiami (OH): 16-41SMU: 5-21ReboundsMiami (OH): 68SMU: 80AssistsMiami (OH): 20SMU: 15TurnoversMiami (OH): 4SMU: 6Points in the paintMiami (OH): 20SMU: 46Largest leadMiami (OH): 14SMU: 4Miami (OH) earned this moment Imagn ImagesMiami (OH) is a throwback mid-major team that stayed together in the transfer portal era, got better and plays a fun style of basketball. It’s great they’ll get to play on the biggest stage now.
